FizzBev Holdings - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the FizzBev Holdings Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A, please press *1 to ask a question, followed by your name. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Vice President of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss FizzBev Holdings' Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Marcus Hale, Chief Financial Officer; Priya Singh, Chief Growth Officer; and Roberto Kline, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Elena.

Elena Vasquez (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on eight key areas: market share trends for major brands, organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter/year, overall company performance highlights, organic revenue growth overall and by region, gross margin analysis drivers and trends, discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies, EPS guidance and key assumptions, and performance of key brands and product categories.

First, regarding market share trends for major brands: Drawing from the latest NielsenIQ and IRI scan data through the end of September, we're pleased FizzBev continued to outpace the industry, gaining 150 basis points year-over-year in total beverage market share to 24.8% in measured channels across North America. This is our seventh straight quarter of share gains, powered by volume velocity gains, disciplined pricing, and fast innovation in functional beverages and RTD hydration.

In carbonated soft drinks, our biggest franchise at 45% of portfolio revenue, we grew to 29.2% share, up 80 basis points, grabbing 1.1 points from rivals. FizzCola led with a 2.3 point gain to 18.7%, thanks to the Zero Sugar Revolution relaunch using stevia and monk fruit for zero added sugars while keeping the bold taste. It boosted household penetration 4.2 points among health-focused Gen Z, per IRI. Meanwhile, Coca-Cola's core slipped 0.5 points to 42.1%, and PepsiCo stayed flat at 21.4% due to convenience channel issues.

In energy drinks, a $28 billion category at 8% CAGR, Surge Energy hit 14.5% share, up 220 basis points. Surge Zero, with 150mg natural caffeine from green tea and B-vitamins, reached 12% ACV in 12 weeks, taking 0.8 points from Monster's 38.2% and Red Bull's 32.7%. Targeted TikTok and Spotify ads for women drove 15% of new occasions, and c-store cooler share rose to 22% from 18%.

Non-carbonateds showed hydration and RTD tea/coffee strength despite 2% category dip. FizzPure Hydration reached 11.8%, up 90 basis points, with sparkling electrolyte variants at 35% of sales over $2.99 ASP, beating Gatorade's 26.4% decline and BodyArmor's flat 9.2%. In North America, 55% of bev sales, we gained 2.1 points to 27.3%, strong in Southeast via NASCAR for FizzCola.

EMEA, 20% of revenue, gained 60 basis points to 18.4% despite 5% UK/Germany inflation, led by FizzFit probiotics eroding Perrier. APAC, 15% mix, exploded 4.2 points to 12.7%, with FizzTea at 8.5% in Thailand/India via cold-chain to 85% modern trade ACV, vs. Lipton's 1.2% drop. China FizzEnergy at 2.1% vs. Red Bull's 45%, but Tier-2 pilots at 25% trial.

Snacks, 25% revenue, up 1.8 points to 16.2% globally; FizzCrunch baked chips hit 13.4% savory share vs. Lay's 28.6% dip. LATAM, 10%, +110 bps to 14.9%, FizzCola Mexico at 22% vs. Coke's 48%.

Velocity 2025 invests $500M in distribution, AI assortment, sustainability; SAP tools cut stock-outs 22%, velocity +5-8%; stevia farms de-risk, +12% clean label ASP. NPD 15 Q4 launches defend premiums vs. 14% private label. Q4 +100-150 bps expected with holiday media $200M; risks aluminum +8%, HFCS regs hedged. Share widens our moat for EPS.

Second, concerning organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter/year: For Q4 fiscal 2024, we guide 5% to 7% organic sales growth, accelerating from Q3's 4.2%, via pricing and innovation. FY2025 4% to 6%, high end of 4.5% consensus.

Pricing adds 2-3 points; passed 70% inflation, COGS now 1.5% vs. Q1 4%, hedged 85% cocoa/sugar/dairy to mid-2025. Snacks +1-2% on VitaCrunch.

Volume/mix 2-4 points; bev +5.3% Q3 on PureThirst/GreenSip, +1.2 ACV to 92%; premium mix +50-75 bps per Circana.

Segments: Bevs 4-6% Q4/5% FY25 on BrewBoost $150M; Snacks 6-8%/5-7%; Dairy alts 7-9%/6-8% despite oat tightness.

Regions: NA 5-7%/4-6%, QSR +8%, e-com 18%; Europe 3-5% on EcoSip; APAC/LATAM 7-9%/6-8%, $50M APAC capex.

Pillars: innovation 20% 2025 sales, AI flavors -30% R&D; supply resilience -15% WC days; prune $100M low-margin CSDs.

Watch palm oil, 50 bps FX drag; tailwinds CPI 3.2%, wages.

Third, in terms of overall company performance highlights: Net revenues hit $2.85 billion, +7.2%, ninth straight quarter up. Organic 4.8% (2.1% vol, 2.7% price), +2.1% FX, 0.3% M&A; ex-Asia disruptions, 5.2% vs. industry 3.1%. Premiums +18% vol offset CSD softness.

Adjusted gross margins +210 bps to 38.4% on $85M COGS savings (palm -15% RSPO), offset 4.2% inflation. EBITDA $620M +12%, margins +140 bps to 21.8%; EPS $1.42 +10%, $250M buybacks at $68 avg.

Snacks 42% rev +9% org, CrispWave +1.2 MMS vs. Frito-Lay, -25% sodium. Bevs 35% +5%, hydration +14%; Conv Foods +4%, e-com 18%.

Regions: NA 55% +8.5% club velocity; EMEA +6% upcycled R&D; APAC 18% +3% India 12%; LATAM +5% hedged.

AI forecasting -12% inv, -8% waste $45M; 95% recyclable pack +7 NPS; drone ag -22% water. Net debt/EBITDA 2.1x, OCF $750M, CapEx $400M Texas line; FCF 95%, div +12% to $0.48.

Harvest Forward: premiumize, innovate wellness, efficiency for FY24 4-6% org, 22%+ EBITDA.

Fourth, looking at organic revenue growth overall and by region: Organic revenue grew 5.2% YoY constant currency, beating 3-5% guide, best since pre-pandemic. Ex-1.8% FX, divested confec. 2.9% vol, 1.7% price/mix, 0.6% channels; pricing 4.2% offset cocoa/sugar/dairy now 5-7% hedged 80% H2; premium/functional +12% to 28% sales.

NA 55% +7.1%: 4.2% vol, CleanSip +18% vs. VitH2O/Gatorade Zero; +2.9% price club; regen corn -8% cost, +150 bps func share 14.2%.

EMEA 20% +3.8%: 1.5% vol HarvestCrunch +22% vs. Oreo; +2.3% price dairy; Digital Shelf +35% online, +80 bps Germany oat lattes.

APAC 15% +6.4%: 5.1% vol coconut +30% 7-Elevens; +1.3% price Indonesia pouches; AI inv -40% stockouts.

LATAM 10% +2.9%: flat vol +4.5% price TropiFuel +15% vs. Guaraná; micro-hubs +12% rural, fair-trade mangoes.

Sustain 4-6% FY24 on $120M R&D 15 launches, Zero-Waste -25% pack, probiotics.

Fifth, reviewing gross margin analysis drivers and trends: Consolidated gross margin 48.2%, +140 bps YoY from 46.8%, flat seq from 48.3%; sixth straight expansion, TTM 47.5% vs. industry 42%.

Gross profit +9% to $1.42B on 5% rev; +320 bps pricing offset 180 bps inflation; const FX 48.7%.

Pricing +8.2% avg, 60% snacks/bevs, +12% premiums no vol loss; EDLP +4% value.

Mix +110 bps: premium/func 42% from 38%; OatFlex +25% at 55% vs. dairy 38%.

Supply eff +90 bps: raws +6% wheat/cocoa/oil hedged cocoa $4200 vs $6800 save $45M; nearshoring -30% freight; robotics -18% labor.

Regions: NA 51.4% +200 bps snacks; Europe 45.2% +100 bps cocoa fixed; APAC/LATAM 42.1% flat, India tea +150 bps.

Trends +2.1 pts 3yr CAGR > Coke/Nestlé; Q4 48.5-49.0%, FY 48.0% +120 bps.

Init: John Deere AI wheat -15% cost; recycled PET -5% pack; prune 15 SKUs +100 bps mix; quinoa stake vs grain infl.

Risks cocoa/freight; $500M hedge buffer for 12-15% op margin 3yr.

Sixth, analyzing discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies: Pricing and RGM drove 5.2% rev +6.1% FX-neutral; +4.1 pts price/mix offset -0.9% vol, third qtr beat peers IRI +2.8%.

Pricing pillars: +4.5% list Q3 > Q2 3.8% wheat/corn; elasticity -0.3 vs -0.4 model Nielsen/Kantar AI; value guardrails <6% no test.

Bevs 55% +5.2% ZestCola aluminum +8%, RTD +4.8% func $15B; snacks +3.9% BFY +6% cocoa $10k/ton.

Geo: NA +5.1% Walmart; EMEA +3.7% HFSS/deposits; APAC +6.3% urban.

ASP +4.2% 80% uplift; Q4 3-5% e-com.

Mix +2.1% MMG 42.3% +110 bps; premiums 28% +; 12 SKUs $45M 60% attach; prune 8% low-ROI +1.5 BFY plant +18%; AFH 22% +300 bps QSR +7%; e-com 12% +22% AOV +14%.

RGM cockpit SAP/ML 3.2x ROI; NutriRewards 8M users +5% repeat.

Vol -0.9% core flat; NA +1.2 BFY; EMEA -1.1 protein +4 Ozempic; APAC/LATAM +3.5 RTD +12.

FY24 4-6% price/mix Q4 dynamic IRI; sustain +2% recyclable EU; risks tariffs/cocoa 85% contracts.

RGM for mid-single rev vs 2-3% cat headwinds.

Seventh, examining EPS guidance and key assumptions: FY2024 adjusted EPS $3.45-$3.55, narrowed from $3.35-$3.55, +8% mid vs $3.20 2023, 5% org net FX.

Rev $12.8-$13.0B +4% mid; org 4-5% 3% price 1-2% vol/mix; Q4 +2% EM pricing.

Vol stab NA conv/club +12% NutriCrunch #2 protein chips; mix +150 bps premium 28%; e-com 15%.

Regions: NA mid-single salty share; EMEA flat-1% +4% price; APAC/LATAM high-single Indo tea +18 Mexico +3 vs Red Bull.

FX -1%; M&A +50 bps $250M EuroVeg.

Gross 38.5-39.0% +120 bps; infl low-mid single hedged palm 80%; $150M savings 105% precision ag -15% waste SAP 8.2x turns.

SG&A 22.5-23% $80M ZBB offshoring; mktg 65% digital TikTok PlantPower -50% sugar; innov +10% upcycled bars ESG.

Interest $120M debt 2.2x; tax 24%; shares 285M $400M buybacks $45 avg.

Upside Europe recov cocoa <$8k; down 2% vol -3c; geo war-room.

Premiumize prune 5% low e.g. cookies; R&D $200M microbiome; 50% recyclable >Nestlé; ROIC 12% vs peers.

Investor Day Feb 2025-27.

Eighth, considering performance of key brands and product categories: Consolidated rev $4.7B +8.2%, org 5.1% 2.6 vol/mix 2.5 price; 11th qtr >3.8% ind; margins +140 bps 38.7% despite 12-15% cocoa/sugar/palm.

Bevs 42% +9.5% org; Zest Hydrate +7.2% vol +110 bps 24.8% $12B sports vs Gatorade, Zero Sugar <5g monk/stevia; +4.1% ASP func RTD; APAC +12% mango/lychee 15% CAGR.

Snacks 31% +7.8%; CrunchWave +10.2% 6.5% vol +90 bps 18.2% savory air-fried -40% fat; 65% recyclable e-com 22% + TikTok; +3.7% price priv label.

Health/Wellness 15% +14.3%; VitaBloom +11.8% vol +250 bps 9.7% $8B alt-dairy pea prot ferment -30% cost; RTD shakes vs Muscle Milk; margins +280 bps 42.1% WI plant.

Conv Foods 12% +6.2%; QuickForge +8.4% EMEA vs HelloFresh; LATAM Brazil -2.1% vol +4.1% const FX.

Regions: NA 62% growth +10.1% IRI; EMEA +7.3% Tesco; APAC +12.6% China +28% Tmall low-cal; LATAM +3.8% hedge 90% local -18% duties.

Vitality: 85% growth health; R&D $220M 4.8% AI flavors regen cocoa Barry -20% yields; divest $450M tuck-in Korean kombucha.

Q4 6-8% org +100 bps MMS mid-teens EPS.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Marcus to provide more detail on our financial results.

Marcus Hale (CFO):
Thank you, Elena. As Elena mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3. Net sales were $2.85 billion, representing a 7.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.4%, impacted by input cost inflation offset by pricing and efficiencies. Operating income was $450 million, and earnings per share were $1.42. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.2 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for 4% to 6% organic growth and adjusted EPS of $3.45 to $3.55.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Doe (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Elena Vasquez (CEO):
Thanks, John. Inflation remains elevated in commodities like cocoa up 22%, sugar, dairy, and aluminum at 8%, totaling 4-6% COGS impact. We've passed through 70% via targeted 4-5% pricing, hedged 80-85% key inputs to mid-2025, and driven efficiencies like nearshoring and AI inventory to save $85M in COGS. This kept gross margins expanding 140-210 bps while sustaining volume/mix. We're monitoring El Niño palm risks but insulated by North America focus and regen sourcing.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Sarah Lee (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for Surge Zero and what is the expected impact of the product?

Priya Singh (Chief Growth Officer):
Great question, Sarah. Surge Zero is a cornerstone of our functional energy push, with 150mg natural caffeine, B-vits, targeting women and all-day focus. In 12 weeks, 12% ACV, stealing 0.8 share points from Monster/Red Bull via TikTok/Spotify, 15% new occasions. Plans include Q4 expansion to 25% ACV, cooler dominance to 22% c-stores, and variants. Expect $150M run-rate FY25, +2-3% to bev organic growth, 14.5% cat share.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Mike Patel (JPMorgan):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Roberto Kline (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Thanks, Mike. Disruptions from Red Sea, bird flu, Ukraine persist, but we've cut stock-outs 22-40% with SAP IBP AI demand sensing at 70% plants, robotics -18% labor, nearshoring 20% LATAM to US -30% freight. Regen ag 50k acres stevia/palm, John Deere drones -22% water, vendor-managed inv -15% WC days. Traceability RSPO cocoa, quinoa stake hedge grains. This saved $45-85M COGS, supports velocity +5-8%, positions for Q4 holiday.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Emily Chen with Barclays. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Marcus Hale (CFO):
Emily, for Q4 and FY24 closeout, organic sales 5-7% Q4, full year 4-6%; gross margins 48.5-49%, EPS $3.45-3.55 mid +8%. Drivers: pricing 2-3 pts, vol/mix 2-4, innovation 20% sales, e-com 18%, premiums 28%. Risks FX 50bps, commodities moderated; tailwinds wage growth, AFH recovery. FY25 organic 4-6%, share +100-150 bps, ROIC 12%. Confident execution.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Elena for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in FizzBev Holdings. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
